plan.topic: Knees aching less since losing weight on semaglutide (Wegovy)? What the STEP 9 randomized knee-osteoarthritis trial found
plan.angle:
13:00 felt-moment Short, careful and evidence-first.
- Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer) names semaglutide. It gives the relief fact as one rounded result: in STEP 9, adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis had a bigger drop in knee pain on semaglutide than on placebo over 68 weeks. Copy the WOMAC pain change for both arms from NEJM 2024 (PubMed). Put the population, the measure and the per-arm sizes on screen.
- One line: weight loss lowers the load on the knees, as 'likely partly because' and never as proven cause.
- Weight is one health measure among many. Semaglutide isn't approved to treat osteoarthritis, so ask your clinician about knee care.
- No retatrutide, no pipeline drugs and no news framing.
- Closing: the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', then the loop line. 160 words or fewer.
- Post note: the target is the Side Effects long video.
plan.working_title: Semaglutide (Wegovy) and Knee Pain: Real Relief? #shorts
plan.why: Knee pain and GLP-1s is moving into mainstream health news. This rides the trend early with a felt symptom on an approved drug and a randomized trial, not the unapproved retatrutide.

package.title: Semaglutide (Wegovy) Beat Placebo on Knee Pain in STEP 9 #shorts
package.description:
Semaglutide (Wegovy) eased knee pain more than placebo over 68 weeks in STEP 9, a randomized trial in adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis — on top of diet and activity counseling for both groups.
Whatever your knees are doing, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Semaglutide #KneeOsteoarthritis #STEP9
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Semaglutide's knee relief wasn't just placebo 🦵

In STEP 9, a randomized trial, adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis took semaglutide (Wegovy) or a placebo — both groups also got diet and activity counseling.

On a 100-point pain scale, knee pain fell about 42 points on semaglutide vs about 28 on placebo over 68 weeks.

Semaglutide led to much greater weight loss, and less weight on the joints likely explains part of that extra relief.

Semaglutide isn't approved to treat osteoarthritis, so knee care is still its own conversation with your clinician.

Save this for anyone asking about weight and knee pain.

Whatever your knees are doing, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

#Semaglutide #KneeOsteoarthritis #STEP9

script.cta: Spoken close: "Whatever your knees are doing, don't stop or change your medicine on your own." then "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber." then the loop line "So when the stairs feel easier, remember what the trial found." This runs into "Semaglutide's knee relief wasn't just placebo." There is no subscribe line and no link line. Post note (Exp G): the watch-next target is the Side Effects long video. Word count: 156, counting hyphenated words as one (standard arm, 135–160). Source note: src3 (Wegovy Prescribing Information) was removed because its printed revised date couldn't be checked in the PDF during this revision, and a guessed date would be a placeholder. The fact-checker has already confirmed the s05 line "Semaglutide isn't approved to treat osteoarthritis" as correct. If a verified label citation is needed, re-add the Wegovy PI with the "Revised: MM/YYYY" date read from https://www.novo-pi.com/wegovy.pdf and tag it to s05.

factcheck.summary: This Short is accurate and safe to ship, with five small wording fixes listed below. I checked every STEP 9 number in it against the trial: 407 adults with obesity and moderate knee osteoarthritis (NEJM 2024;391:1573-1583, NCT05064735, funded by Novo Nordisk). Pain on the WOMAC scale (0–100) fell 41.7 points on semaglutide vs 27.5 on placebo at week 68. Body weight fell 13.7% vs 3.2%. Both groups got counselling on a reduced-calorie diet and physical activity. All of these match the script, and the rounded spoken numbers (about 42 and about 28) are faithful. The 2005 Messier knee-load study exists and backs "less weight means less load on the knees". The script hedges the weight explanation ("likely partly"), which is right, because STEP 9 didn't test whether weight loss explains the pain relief. "Not approved to treat osteoarthritis" is correct for Wegovy. The scoped don't-stop line and the required safety card are both there, with no subscribe or link line. The topic needs no emergency line. The minor issues: the hook "isn't a fluke" suggests the result has been repeated, but it comes from one trial. The first spoken number has no comparator in its own sentence. The s02 card can't be understood with the sound off. The label source has a bare year. The word count is off by three but still inside the arm.

issues.claim: Semaglutide knee relief isn't a fluke.
issues.problem: "Isn't a fluke" suggests the result has been confirmed more than once, but the evidence is a single trial (STEP 9) funded by the drug's maker. A wording that keeps the negation hook but matches what was actually shown is safer.
issues.fix: Narration: "Semaglutide's knee relief wasn't just placebo. In a randomized trial, knee pain eased more on semaglutide than on placebo over sixty-eight weeks." On-screen: "Semaglutide's knee relief wasn't just placebo". Also update the s08 loop note so it runs into this new first sentence.

issues.claim: knee pain fell an average of about forty-two points on semaglutide.
issues.problem: The rule is that every spoken number names its comparator. The placebo figure only comes in s03, so anyone who swipes away after s02 hears the semaglutide drop with nothing to compare it to.
issues.fix: "On a hundred-point scale, knee pain fell an average of about forty-two points on semaglutide, versus about twenty-eight on placebo." Then shorten s03 to: "So the placebo group improved too. Both groups got diet and activity counseling, so semaglutide's extra relief came on top of that."

issues.problem: The card fails the muted-viewer test. It doesn't say which drug, which group is which, the measure, the population or the timeframe. That detail is only in the visual fact field.
issues.fix: On-screen: "STEP 9 knee pain (WOMAC), 68 weeks: semaglutide −41.7 vs placebo −27.5", and keep the population line "Adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis" visible on the stat card.

issues.problem: The source has only a bare year. The rule requires the label's real revised date, checked in the PDF.
issues.fix: Open https://www.novo-pi.com/wegovy.pdf and replace "2025" with the "Revised: MM/YYYY" date printed on the label.

issues.problem: My count of the narration is about 151 words. That is still inside the standard arm (135–160), but the stated number is wrong. If you apply the s02 fix (+5 words) and the s03 change (−4 words), the total stays at about 152.
issues.fix: Recount after the edits and update the note, e.g. "Word count: 152 (standard arm, 135–160)."
